```{r blind-switch}
UNBLIND <- as.logical(Sys.getenv("UNBLIND_STUDY2", "FALSE"))
# The blind switch. UNBLIND is FALSE unless the environment variable
# UNBLIND_STUDY2 (a named setting the operating system passes to R) is set to
# TRUE. While it is FALSE, the labels are shuffled right after the data are
# built (section 3), and every output goes to a blind_run/ subfolder of the
# folder its real counterpart goes to. A value that is neither TRUE nor FALSE
# stops the run, so a typing error cannot unblind it.
if (is.na(UNBLIND)) stop("UNBLIND_STUDY2 must be TRUE or FALSE.")

# A blind report belongs in blind_run/, and an unblinded report beside this
# file. The knit: line in the header reads the same environment variable and
# sends the report to the right folder when the file is knitted with
# RStudio's Knit button. A call to rmarkdown::render() must pass
# output_dir = "blind_run" in a blind run and leave it out in an unblinded
# run. A run whose report would land in the wrong folder stops here, before
# anything is written. The folder is read from the settings render() is
# running with; a knit that does not go through render() is not checked.
render_output_dir <- function() {
  frame <- Find(function(e) exists("output_dir", envir = e, inherits = FALSE) &&
                  exists("knit_input", envir = e, inherits = FALSE),
                sys.frames())
  if (is.null(frame)) return(NULL)
  d <- get("output_dir", envir = frame)
  normalizePath(if (is.null(d)) "." else d, mustWork = FALSE)
}
report_dir <- render_output_dir()
if (!UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) != "blind_run") {
  stop("A blind report must be written to blind_run/. Knit with the Knit ",
       "button, or run rmarkdown::render(\"Study2_01_Quant.Rmd\", ",
       "output_dir = \"blind_run\").")
}
if (UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) == "blind_run") {
  stop("An unblinded report must not be written to blind_run/. Set the ",
       "environment variable UNBLIND_STUDY2 to TRUE before knitting, or run ",
       "rmarkdown::render(\"Study2_01_Quant.Rmd\") without output_dir.")
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      fig.align = "center")
```

```{r banner, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (!UNBLIND) {
  cat("**Blind run. The source labels are shuffled across participants, the",
      "modification labels across the versions of each source image that a",
      "participant saw, and the image-kind labels across the ten source",

} else {

}
```

# 0. What this file does

In Study 1, telling participants that the artist Alex made an artwork by
prompting an AI system lowered its rated creativity. Study 2 asks whether that
penalty reaches a second work that Alex makes by hand from the first. Three
accounts give different answers. If an AI origin taints whatever is built on
it, the penalty holds at every level of modification. If raters judge the
second work partly by the first, the penalty is largest when the second work
is the first unchanged and shrinks as Alex changes more. If raters judge only
what Alex added, the penalty is absent.

Each participant was told that Alex made the ten first works either with
graphic design software and digital sketching tools (Human) or by writing
prompts for an AI system (AI), and that he made every second work himself
with design tools. Each participant then saw every source image at three
levels of modification: None (the first work shown again unchanged), Slight
(colour and contrast adjustments) and Dramatic (substantial changes by hand).
After each second work they rated how transformative it is compared to the
first, how much the first work's essence changed, and how much creativity went
into it, and wrote a justification after every rating.

The registration (`Docs/Preregistration/AsPredicted/Study2_AsPredicted.md`)
is the specification for everything below. This file:

1. reads the two Qualtrics exports and the survey file and applies the five
   registered exclusion steps in order (section 2);
2. scores each rating by its position on the answer scale, builds the long
   data, checks every count the registration states, and drops the two
   six-point items (section 2);
3. shuffles the labels in a blind run and writes the long data file (section 3);
4. fits the registered model on each measure and runs the four registered
   tests per measure, twelve in one Holm family, with the equivalence test of
   the source penalty (section 5);
5. checks tests 1, 2 and 4 with cumulative-link models (section 6);
6. gives the exploratory source contrast at each modification level
   (section 7);
7. records the status of every fit and the run (sections 8 and 9).

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r packages}
# dplyr, tidyr, tibble and readr build and write the tables. lme4 fits the
# linear mixed models, regressions that give each participant and each source
# image its own baseline, and lmerTest supplies Satterthwaite degrees of
# freedom (an approximation to the degrees of freedom a test in a mixed model
# has). emmeans gives estimated marginal means, the model's predicted mean for
# each condition averaged equally over the other factors, and the contrasts
# between them. ordinal fits the cumulative-link mixed models of section 6.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(readr)
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(emmeans)
  library(ordinal)
})
```

## 1.2 Paths and registered constants

```{r paths}
# Every path is found from this file's own folder, which is the working
# directory when the file is knitted. Three environment variables override
# the defaults:
#   STUDY2_DIR           the Study 2 folder, where the outputs go
#   STUDY_SHARED_R       the folder of the shared R helpers
#   STUDY2_PROJECT_ROOT  the project root, the folder that holds Data and
#                        Analysis
# Printed paths are relative to the Study 2 folder or the project root, so no
# printed line names a folder particular to one machine.
STUDY_DIR <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("STUDY2_DIR", getwd()), mustWork = TRUE)
SHARED_R  <- Sys.getenv("STUDY_SHARED_R",
                        file.path(STUDY_DIR, "..", "shared", "R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "fit_status.R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "qualtrics_import.R"))

PROJECT_ROOT <- find_project_root(start = STUDY_DIR,
                                  env_var = "STUDY2_PROJECT_ROOT")
EXPORTS <- study_export_paths(PROJECT_ROOT, 2)

# A blind run writes each file to a blind_run/ subfolder of the folder its
# real counterpart goes to.
mode_dir <- function(dir) if (UNBLIND) dir else file.path(dir, "blind_run")
OUT_STUDY  <- mode_dir(STUDY_DIR)
OUT_TABLES <- mode_dir(file.path(STUDY_DIR, "tables"))
for (p in c(OUT_STUDY, OUT_TABLES)) {
  dir.create(p, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

cat("Values export: ", relative_path(EXPORTS$values, PROJECT_ROOT), "\n")
cat("Labels export: ", relative_path(EXPORTS$labels, PROJECT_ROOT), "\n")
cat("Survey file:   ", relative_path(EXPORTS$qsf, PROJECT_ROOT), "\n")
cat("Long data to:  ", relative_path(OUT_STUDY, STUDY_DIR), "\n")
cat("Tables to:     ", relative_path(OUT_TABLES, STUDY_DIR), "\n")

# The registered constants.
SEED          <- 20260421L  # the Study 1 seed, used for every shuffle
EQ_BOUND      <- 0.224      # half the 0.448-point Study 1 creativity penalty
ALPHA         <- 0.05
N_FAMILY      <- 12L        # four tests on each of three measures
MEASURES      <- c("transformativeness", "essence_change", "creativity")
SOURCE_LEVELS <- c("Human", "AI")
MOD_LEVELS    <- c("None", "Slight", "Dramatic")
KIND_LEVELS   <- c("Figure", "NonFigure")
SIX_POINT_ITEMS <- c("1NonFigureNoneTrans", "1NonFigureMinTrans")
TASK_ANSWER   <- "Viewing images for a set amount of time and answering questions"
```

## 1.3 Run record

```{r run-record}
# The run record ties every output to this run. It stores the SHA-256
# checksum of each input (a 64-character fingerprint of the file's exact
# bytes), deletes the previous run's manifest now, deletes each output's
# previous copy before the chunk that writes it, and writes the manifest
# last. A manifest on disk therefore means the run reached its end.
run <- start_run_record(
  c(values_export = EXPORTS$values,
    labels_export = EXPORTS$labels,
    survey_file   = EXPORTS$qsf),
  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_quant_run_manifest.csv"),
  STUDY_DIR)
write_run_inputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_quant_run_inputs.csv"))
cat("Run identifier:", run$run_id, "\n")
print(as.data.frame(run$inputs[, c("input", "file", "bytes", "sha256")]))

if (!UNBLIND) {
  # A short note in each blind folder says what the folder holds.
  blind_notes <- file.path(c(OUT_STUDY, OUT_TABLES), "BLIND_RUN.txt")
  run_clear_outputs(run, blind_notes)
  for (f in blind_notes) {
    writeLines(c(
      "Outputs of a blind run of the Study 2 pipeline.",
      "The source labels were shuffled across participants, the modification",
      "labels across the versions of each source image a participant saw, and",
      "the image-kind labels across the ten source images, before any summary",
      "or model. Study2_03_Integration.Rmd also shuffles the ratings across the",
      "responses to each question before it relates any word to a rating. No",
      "number in this folder describes the real conditions or the real link",
      "between the words and the ratings. A run with UNBLIND_STUDY2 set to TRUE",
      "writes the real outputs one folder up."), f)
  }
}
```

# 2. Import, exclusions and the registered counts

## 2.1 The exclusion flow

```{r exclusions}
# Qualtrics, the survey platform, exports the study twice: the Values export
# holds raw choice codes and the Labels export holds the text each
# participant saw. read_qualtrics_pair() reads both and checks that they hold
# the same records in the same order.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_exclusion_flow.csv"))

ex <- read_qualtrics_pair(EXPORTS$values, EXPORTS$labels)
stopifnot(all(trim_answer(ex$labels$Status) %in% c("IP Address", "Survey Preview")))

# The registered steps, in the order of registration question 6. Each step
# returns TRUE for the records it keeps. Survey Preview records are the
# survey test runs. A blank seriousness answer counts as an answer other than
# "Yes, I did". A blank arithmetic answer passes. The condition is the
# embedded Type field.
steps <- list(
  "survey test runs (Status is Survey Preview)" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(l$Status) == "IP Address",
  "unfinished sessions" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(l$Finished) == "True",
  "seriousness answer other than Yes, I did (blanks included)" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(l$Seriousness) == "Yes, I did",
  "wrong answer to What does 8+7 equal? (a blank passes)" =
    function(v, l) {
      a <- trim_answer(l$AttentionCheck2)
      a == "" | a == "15"
    },
  "no recorded condition" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(l$Type) %in% SOURCE_LEVELS
)
flow <- exclusion_flow(ex$values, ex$labels, steps)

# One line per step, so the flow can be read off the report.
ff <- flow$flow
cat("Records in the export:", ff$n[1], "\n")
for (i in 2:nrow(ff)) {
  cat(sprintf("Step %d, %s: %d -> %d (%d removed)\n",
              i - 1, ff$step[i], ff$n[i - 1], ff$n[i], ff$removed[i]))
}

# The counts the registration states. The run stops if the exports give
# anything else.
REGISTERED_FLOW <- c(275L, 275L, 244L, 235L, 235L, 235L)
ff$registered_n <- REGISTERED_FLOW
if (!identical(as.integer(ff$n), REGISTERED_FLOW)) {
  stop("The exclusion flow does not match the registration: ",
       paste(ff$n, collapse = " -> "), " against ",
       paste(REGISTERED_FLOW, collapse = " -> "), ".")
}
write_csv(ff, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_exclusion_flow.csv"))

# The arithmetic step lets a blank answer pass. The number of blanks that
# reach it is printed, so the report shows whether the rule mattered.
after3 <- exclusion_flow(ex$values, ex$labels, steps[1:3])
n_blank_arith <- sum(trim_answer(after3$labels$AttentionCheck2) == "")
cat("Blank answers to the arithmetic question at step 4:", n_blank_arith, "\n")

# The task question never ended a session, so it is not a criterion. The
# registration states that all 235 answered it correctly.
n_task_right <- sum(trim_answer(flow$labels$AttentionCheck) == TASK_ANSWER)
cat("Correct answers to the task question:", n_task_right, "of",
    nrow(flow$labels), "\n")
```

## 2.2 Scoring by position

```{r scoring}
# Each rating is scored 1 to k by the position of its label among the item's
# answer options, read from the survey file in the order they were shown,
# because the numeric export stores raw choice codes rather than scale
# positions. read_item_scales() leaves out the questions in the survey's
# Trash block, deleted before launch, among them a duplicate 1FigureMaxCreat
# (QID28). An answer whose label is not among the item's options is scored NA
# and listed in the log.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_item_scales.csv"))

scales <- read_item_scales(EXPORTS$qsf, ITEM_FAMILIES$derivative$pattern)
cat("Rating items:", nrow(scales), "| five-point:", sum(scales$k == 5),
    "| six-point:", sum(scales$k == 6), "\n")
cat("Six-point items:", paste(scales$item[scales$k == 6], collapse = ", "), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(scales) == 90, all(scales$k %in% c(5L, 6L)),
          setequal(scales$item[scales$k == 6], SIX_POINT_ITEMS))
write_csv(select(scales, item, question_id, k, anchors, stem),
          file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_item_scales.csv"))

# One row per participant and rating item, with the rating scored by
# position and the written justification that followed it. The justification
# column ends in Resp, Re or R, which varies from item to item.
built <- reshape_ratings_long(flow$values, flow$labels, scales, "derivative",
                              carry_values = "Type")
cat("Rows:", nrow(built$long), "| answers that could not be scored:",
    nrow(built$unscored), "\n")
if (nrow(built$unscored) > 0) {
  print(as.data.frame(built$unscored))
  stop("Some recorded answer could not be scored by position.")
}
```

## 2.3 The long data and the registered counts

```{r long-data}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_sample_checks.csv"))

# The analysis columns. image is the source image, such as 3NonFigure, and
# work_id names the second work, one source image at one modification level,
# such as 3NonFigure_Slight. image and work_id name what was shown and are
# never shuffled. image_kind (Figure when the image shows a human or humanoid
# figure, NonFigure otherwise) and modification are the labels the models
# use, and a blind run shuffles them in section 3.
long_all <- built$long %>%
  transmute(id, source = Type, image = stimulus_id, image_kind = stimulus_type,
            modification, work_id = paste0(stimulus_id, "_", modification),
            dimension, item, k_points, rating, rating_label,
            response_text = justification)

# The design of registration question 4. Every participant saw all ten source
# images, five with a figure and five without, each at the three modification
# levels, which makes 30 second works. Seven participants lack the trial
# 1FigureMin, the first figure image at Slight, and so saw 29.
ALL_WORKS <- as.vector(outer(unique(long_all$image), MOD_LEVELS, paste, sep = "_"))
design <- long_all %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(n_images    = n_distinct(image),
            n_figure    = n_distinct(image[image_kind == "Figure"]),
            n_nonfigure = n_distinct(image[image_kind == "NonFigure"]),
            n_works     = n_distinct(work_id),
            missing     = paste(setdiff(ALL_WORKS, work_id), collapse = " "),
            n_rated     = sum(!is.na(rating)),
            n_justified = sum(response_text != ""),
            .groups = "drop")
answers_per_work <- long_all %>% count(id, work_id, name = "n_answers")

participants <- distinct(long_all, id, source)
sample_checks <- tribble(
  ~quantity,                                                 ~registered, ~observed,
  "participants",                                            235L,   nrow(participants),
  "participants in the Human condition",                     122L,   sum(participants$source == "Human"),
  "participants in the AI condition",                        113L,   sum(participants$source == "AI"),
  "correct answers to the task question",                    235L,   n_task_right,
  "participants who saw all ten source images",              235L,   sum(design$n_images == 10),
  "participants who saw five Figure and five NonFigure images", 235L, sum(design$n_figure == 5 & design$n_nonfigure == 5),
  "participants with 90 ratings",                            228L,   sum(design$n_rated == 90),
  "participants with 87 ratings",                            7L,     sum(design$n_rated == 87),
  "participants lacking the trial 1FigureMin and only it",   7L,     sum(design$missing == "1Figure_Slight"),
  "ratings",                                                 21129L, sum(!is.na(long_all$rating)),
  "justifications",                                          21129L, sum(long_all$response_text != ""),
  "ratings on the two six-point items, dropped",             470L,   sum(long_all$item %in% SIX_POINT_ITEMS & !is.na(long_all$rating)),
  "justifications on the two six-point items, dropped",      470L,   sum(long_all$item %in% SIX_POINT_ITEMS & long_all$response_text != ""),
  "ratings analysed",                                        20659L, sum(!long_all$item %in% SIX_POINT_ITEMS & !is.na(long_all$rating)),
  "justifications analysed",                                 20659L, sum(!long_all$item %in% SIX_POINT_ITEMS & long_all$response_text != "")
) %>% mutate(match = registered == observed)
print(as.data.frame(sample_checks))
write_csv(sample_checks, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_sample_checks.csv"))
if (!all(sample_checks$match)) stop("The sample does not match the registration.")

# Every row holds a rating and a justification, every participant has 30 or
# 29 second works with three answers each, and only the seven named
# participants lack a work.
stopifnot(all(!is.na(long_all$rating)), all(long_all$response_text != ""),
          all(answers_per_work$n_answers == 3),
          all(design$n_works == 30 | design$missing == "1Figure_Slight"),
          all(design$n_rated == design$n_justified))
cat("Every participant saw all ten source images at all three levels, apart",
    "from the seven who lack 1FigureMin.\n")

# The primary data drop the two six-point transformativeness items with their
# justifications (registration question 6), so every rating left is on five
# points.
long <- long_all %>% filter(!item %in% SIX_POINT_ITEMS)
stopifnot(nrow(long) == 20659, all(long$k_points == 5))
cat("Rows analysed:", nrow(long), "\n")
```

# 3. The blind shuffle and the long data file

```{r blind-shuffle}
# In a blind run the labels are shuffled here, after the data are built and
# before any summary or model.
#
# Source is a between-participant label. blind_shuffle() deals each
# participant another participant's source label, so each condition keeps
# its 122 or 113 participants.
#
# Modification varies within each participant, so a shuffle across
# participants would leave its link to the ratings in place. It is shuffled
# within each participant and source image: the modification labels of that
# participant's versions of the image are dealt again among those versions,
# each version keeping one label for all three of its ratings. Every
# participant keeps the same number of works at each level, and the link
# between a work's level and its ratings is cut.
#
# Image kind is a property of the source image, so the ten image-kind labels
# are dealt again among the ten images, five of each kind as before.
#
# Every shuffle uses the registered seed, takes its units in byte order of
# their identifiers so the result is the same on every machine, and puts the
# random-number state back afterwards.
keep_random_state <- function(expr) {
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  on.exit({
    if (had_seed) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
    else if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)) {
      rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
    }
  }, add = TRUE)
  expr
}

shuffle_modification_within <- function(df, seed) {
  units <- distinct(df, id, image, work_id, modification)
  if (anyDuplicated(units[, c("id", "work_id")]) > 0) {
    stop("Some second work carries more than one modification label.")
  }
  units <- units[order(units$id, units$image, units$work_id, method = "radix"), ]
  key <- paste(units$id, units$image, sep = "\r")
  groups <- split(seq_len(nrow(units)), factor(key, levels = unique(key)))
  new_mod <- keep_random_state({
    set.seed(seed)
    out <- character(nrow(units))
    for (rows in groups) out[rows] <- units$modification[rows][sample.int(length(rows))]
    out
  })
  m <- match(paste(df$id, df$work_id), paste(units$id, units$work_id))
  df$modification <- new_mod[m]
  df
}

shuffle_image_kind <- function(df, seed) {
  units <- distinct(df, image, image_kind)
  if (anyDuplicated(units$image) > 0) stop("Some image carries more than one kind.")
  units <- units[order(units$image, method = "radix"), ]
  new_kind <- keep_random_state({
    set.seed(seed)
    units$image_kind[sample.int(nrow(units))]
  })
  df$image_kind <- new_kind[match(df$image, units$image)]
  df
}

# Two count tables are the same when every column holds the same values.
same_columns <- function(a, b) {
  identical(names(a), names(b)) &&
    all(vapply(names(a), function(n) identical(a[[n]], b[[n]]), logical(1)))
}
per_level_before <- count(distinct(long, id, work_id, modification), id, modification)
kinds_before <- count(distinct(long, image, image_kind), image_kind)
if (!UNBLIND) {
  long <- blind_shuffle(long, "id", "source", seed = SEED)
  long <- shuffle_modification_within(long, seed = SEED)
  long <- shuffle_image_kind(long, seed = SEED)
  # The design survives the shuffle: 122 and 113 participants, the same
  # number of works per participant at each level, and five images of each
  # kind.
  stopifnot(identical(sort(table(distinct(long, id, source)$source)),
                      sort(table(participants$source))),
            same_columns(count(distinct(long, id, work_id, modification), id, modification),
                         per_level_before),
            same_columns(count(distinct(long, image, image_kind), image_kind),
                         kinds_before))
  cat("Blind run: source labels shuffled across participants, modification",
      "labels within each participant and source image, image-kind labels",
      "across the ten images, seed", SEED, "\n")
}

long <- long %>%
  mutate(source       = factor(source, levels = SOURCE_LEVELS),
         modification = factor(modification, levels = MOD_LEVELS),
         image_kind   = factor(image_kind, levels = KIND_LEVELS),
         dimension    = factor(dimension, levels = MEASURES),
         label_mode   = if (UNBLIND) "real" else "shuffled") %>%
  arrange(id, work_id, dimension)
stopifnot(!anyNA(long$source), !anyNA(long$modification),
          !anyNA(long$image_kind), !anyNA(long$dimension))
```

```{r write-long}
# The long data file is the input of Study2_02_Text.ipynb, which reads only
# its identifier, second-work, question and text columns, and of
# Study2_03_Integration.Rmd. It carries the condition and the rating, so in a
# blind run it is written to blind_run/ with the shuffled labels, and its
# label_mode column says "shuffled" on every row.
LONG_PATH <- file.path(OUT_STUDY, "study2_long_with_text.csv")
run_clear_outputs(run, LONG_PATH)
write_csv(long %>% mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character)), LONG_PATH, na = "")
cat("Wrote", relative_path(LONG_PATH, STUDY_DIR), "with", nrow(long),
    "rows | label_mode", unique(long$label_mode), "\n")
```

# 4. Cell counts

```{r cell-counts}
# Counts only: participants per source condition, and ratings per source,
# modification level and measure.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_cell_counts.csv"))
cell_counts <- long %>%
  group_by(source, modification, dimension) %>%
  summarise(participants = n_distinct(id), ratings = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(measure = dimension)
print(as.data.frame(cell_counts))
stopifnot(sum(cell_counts$ratings) == 20659)
write_csv(cell_counts, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_cell_counts.csv"))
```

# 5. The registered models and tests

## 5.1 The fits

```{r fit-models}
# Each measure gets the registered linear mixed model:
#
#   rating ~ source x modification x image kind
#            + (1 | participant) + (1 | source image)
#
# Every factor uses sum-to-zero contrasts, a coding in which a factor's
# effects add to zero across its levels, so each effect is read against the
# average of the other factors. The fit is by restricted maximum likelihood
# (REML, the usual estimator of the variances in a mixed model) with the
# bobyqa optimizer, as in Study 1. fit_with_status() keeps every warning and
# records whether the fit stopped with an error, whether it converged and
# whether it is singular (a variance estimated at zero).
SUM_CONTRASTS <- list(source = "contr.sum", modification = "contr.sum",
                      image_kind = "contr.sum")
FORMULA <- rating ~ source * modification * image_kind + (1 | id) + (1 | image)

model_data <- function(m) {
  long %>%
    filter(dimension == m) %>%
    mutate(id = factor(id), image = factor(image))
}
data_by_measure <- setNames(lapply(MEASURES, model_data), MEASURES)
primary <- lapply(data_by_measure, function(d) {
  fit_with_status(lmerTest::lmer(FORMULA, data = d, REML = TRUE,
                                 contrasts = SUM_CONTRASTS,
                                 control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))
})
for (m in MEASURES) {
  st <- primary[[m]]$status
  cat(m, ": rows", nrow(data_by_measure[[m]]), "| fit error", st$fit_error,
      "| converged", st$converged, "| singular", st$singular, "\n")
}
stopifnot(sum(vapply(data_by_measure, nrow, integer(1))) == 20659)
```

## 5.2 Estimated marginal means

```{r emmeans}
# The model's mean for each modification level, each source condition and
# each source and level together, each averaged equally over the factors not
# named, with 95 percent confidence intervals (the range of means compatible
# with the data). emmeans switches off Satterthwaite degrees of freedom above
# 3,000 observations unless told otherwise; the registration names them, so
# the limit is raised above the size of any model here.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_emmeans.csv"))

emm_of <- function(fit, spec, d) {
  emmeans::emmeans(fit, spec, data = d, lmer.df = "satterthwaite",
                   lmerTest.limit = 25000)
}

GRIDS <- list("modification" = ~ modification, "source" = ~ source,
              "source by modification" = ~ source * modification)
emm_table <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  res <- primary[[m]]
  if (res$status$fit_error) {
    return(tibble(measure = m, note = fit_note(res$status, "mean")))
  }
  bind_rows(lapply(names(GRIDS), function(g) {
    s <- as_tibble(summary(emm_of(res$fit, GRIDS[[g]], data_by_measure[[m]]))) %>%
      mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character))
    for (col in c("source", "modification")) {
      if (!col %in% names(s)) s[[col]] <- NA_character_
    }
    s %>%
      transmute(measure = m, means_of = g, source, modification,
                emmean, se = SE, df,
                ci95_lo = na_unless_usable(lower.CL, res$status),
                ci95_hi = na_unless_usable(upper.CL, res$status),
                averaged_over = "the factors not named, equal weights",
                note = fit_note(res$status, "interval"))
  }))
}))
n_fit_errors <- sum(vapply(primary, function(r) isTRUE(r$status$fit_error), logical(1)))
stopifnot(nrow(emm_table) == 11 * (3 - n_fit_errors) + n_fit_errors)
write_csv(emm_table, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_emmeans.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(emm_table, measure, means_of, source, modification,
                           emmean, se, ci95_lo, ci95_hi)), digits = 4)
```

## 5.3 The four registered tests and the Holm family

```{r confirmatory}
# Four tests per measure, each a contrast between estimated marginal means
# with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom:
#
#   1. Slight minus None, averaged over source and image kind;
#   2. Dramatic minus Slight, averaged the same way. H1 holds on a measure
#      when both are positive and significant;
#   3. Human minus AI, averaged over modification and image kind, by an
#      equivalence test: two one-sided tests of whether the difference lies
#      inside plus or minus 0.224 rating points. One asks whether it lies
#      above -0.224, the other whether it lies below +0.224, and the larger
#      of the two one-sided p-values is the test's p-value;
#   4. Human minus AI at None, minus Human minus AI at Dramatic, two-sided.
#      A positive value means the penalty shrinks as Alex changes more.
#
# Tests 1, 2 and 4 are two-sided t tests. Holm's method corrects the twelve
# p-values together: they are ordered, the smallest is compared with .05
# divided by twelve, the next with .05 divided by eleven, and so on, stopping
# at the first that fails. This holds the chance of any false positive among
# the twelve at .05. The correction is told the family has twelve members
# whatever happens, so a missing p-value never makes it lighter for the
# others.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_confirmatory_family.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_equivalence.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_hypothesis_readings.csv"))

# The contrast weights of test 4, matched to the cells by their labels so
# that no weight depends on the order emmeans lists the cells in.
interaction_weights <- function(grid) {
  cell <- function(s, mo) as.numeric(grid$source == s & grid$modification == mo)
  (cell("Human", "None") - cell("AI", "None")) -
    (cell("Human", "Dramatic") - cell("AI", "Dramatic"))
}

TEST_NAMES <- c(
  "1" = "Slight minus None",
  "2" = "Dramatic minus Slight",
  "3" = "Human minus AI, averaged over modification (equivalence)",
  "4" = "Human minus AI at None, minus Human minus AI at Dramatic")

# The four contrasts of one fit, as one row each. The function takes the
# emmeans call so that the same code serves the cumulative-link models.
four_contrasts <- function(emm) {
  e_mod <- emm(~ modification)
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(e_mod@grid$modification), MOD_LEVELS))
  c12 <- emmeans::contrast(e_mod, list("Slight minus None" = c(-1, 1, 0),
                                       "Dramatic minus Slight" = c(0, -1, 1)),
                           adjust = "none")
  e_src <- emm(~ source)
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(e_src@grid$source), SOURCE_LEVELS))
  c3 <- emmeans::contrast(e_src, list("Human minus AI" = c(1, -1)), adjust = "none")
  e_sm <- emm(~ source * modification)
  w4 <- interaction_weights(e_sm@grid)
  stopifnot(sum(w4 != 0) == 4, sum(w4) == 0)
  c4 <- emmeans::contrast(e_sm, list("interaction" = w4), adjust = "none")
  # emmeans names the interval columns lower.CL and upper.CL when the test
  # has finite degrees of freedom, and asymp.LCL and asymp.UCL when it is a z
  # test, as in the cumulative-link models.
  s <- function(ct, level, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) {
    tab <- as_tibble(summary(ct, infer = infer, level = level))
    names(tab)[names(tab) %in% c("lower.CL", "asymp.LCL")] <- "ci_lo"
    names(tab)[names(tab) %in% c("upper.CL", "asymp.UCL")] <- "ci_hi"
    tab
  }
  rows <- bind_rows(s(c12, 0.95), s(c3, 0.95), s(c4, 0.95))
  stat <- intersect(c("t.ratio", "z.ratio"), names(rows))
  ci90 <- s(c3, 0.90, infer = c(TRUE, FALSE))
  tibble(test = 1:4, estimate = rows$estimate, se = rows$SE, df = rows$df,
         statistic = rows[[stat]], p_two_sided = rows$p.value,
         ci95_lo = rows$ci_lo, ci95_hi = rows$ci_hi,
         ci90_lo = c(NA, NA, ci90$ci_lo, NA),
         ci90_hi = c(NA, NA, ci90$ci_hi, NA),
         equivalence_check = c(NA, NA,
                               as_tibble(summary(emmeans::test(c3, delta = EQ_BOUND,
                                                               side = "equivalence")))$p.value,
                               NA))
}

# The two one-sided tests of test 3, written out. With symmetric bounds the
# larger p-value equals the p-value emmeans gives for side = "equivalence",
# and the run checks that the two agree.
tost <- function(est, se, df, bound) {
  p_lower <- pt((est + bound) / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  p_upper <- pt((est - bound) / se, df, lower.tail = TRUE)
  tibble(p_lower = p_lower, p_upper = p_upper, p_tost = pmax(p_lower, p_upper))
}

test_rows <- function(res, m) {
  base <- tibble(measure = m, test = 1:4, test_name = unname(TEST_NAMES))
  if (res$status$fit_error) {
    return(base %>% mutate(estimate = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, df = NA_real_,
                           statistic = NA_real_, p_two_sided = NA_real_,
                           ci95_lo = NA_real_, ci95_hi = NA_real_,
                           ci90_lo = NA_real_, ci90_hi = NA_real_,
                           p_lower = NA_real_, p_upper = NA_real_,
                           p_family = NA_real_, converged = FALSE,
                           singular = NA, note = fit_note(res$status)))
  }
  d <- data_by_measure[[m]]
  ct <- four_contrasts(function(spec) emm_of(res$fit, spec, d))
  eq <- tost(ct$estimate[3], ct$se[3], ct$df[3], EQ_BOUND)
  stopifnot(abs(eq$p_tost - ct$equivalence_check[3]) < 1e-8)
  base %>%
    bind_cols(select(ct, -test, -equivalence_check)) %>%
    mutate(p_lower = c(NA, NA, eq$p_lower, NA),
           p_upper = c(NA, NA, eq$p_upper, NA),
           p_family = ifelse(test == 3, eq$p_tost, p_two_sided),
           across(c(p_two_sided, p_lower, p_upper, p_family,
                    ci95_lo, ci95_hi, ci90_lo, ci90_hi),
                  ~ na_unless_usable(.x, res$status)),
           converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
           note = fit_note(res$status))
}

family <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) test_rows(primary[[m]], m))) %>%
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p_family, method = "holm", n = N_FAMILY),
         holm_significant = p_holm < ALPHA,
         reading = case_when(
           is.na(p_holm) ~ NA_character_,
           test %in% 1:2 & holm_significant & estimate > 0 ~ "positive and significant",
           test %in% 1:2 & holm_significant & estimate < 0 ~ "negative and significant",
           test %in% 1:2 ~ "not significant",
           test == 3 & holm_significant ~ "equivalent: inside plus or minus 0.224",
           test == 3 ~ "not shown to lie inside plus or minus 0.224",
           test == 4 & holm_significant & estimate > 0 ~
             "significant and positive: the penalty shrinks from None to Dramatic",
           test == 4 & holm_significant & estimate < 0 ~
             "significant and negative: the penalty grows from None to Dramatic",
           TRUE ~ "not significant"),
         family = "twelve registered tests, Holm, family-wise alpha .05",
         bound = ifelse(test == 3, EQ_BOUND, NA_real_)) %>%
  relocate(p_holm, holm_significant, reading, .after = p_family)
stopifnot(nrow(family) == N_FAMILY)
write_csv(family, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_confirmatory_family.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(family, measure, test, estimate, se, df, p_family,
                           p_holm, reading, converged, singular)), digits = 4)
```

## 5.4 The equivalence tests and the readings of the three hypotheses

```{r readings}
# The equivalence test of each measure, with its 90 percent interval. Both
# one-sided tests pass at .05 exactly when that interval lies inside the
# bound. The registered verdict rests on the Holm-corrected p-value. A pass
# means that less than half of Study 1's creativity penalty reaches a
# second work made by hand. A fail means only that the penalty is not shown
# to be small.
equivalence <- family %>%
  filter(test == 3) %>%
  transmute(measure, contrast = test_name, estimate, se, df, ci90_lo, ci90_hi,
            bound, p_lower, p_upper, p_tost = p_family, p_holm,
            equivalent = holm_significant,
            interval_inside_bound = ci90_lo > -bound & ci90_hi < bound,
            reading, converged, singular, note)
stopifnot(nrow(equivalence) == 3)
write_csv(equivalence, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_equivalence.csv"))

# The three hypotheses, read on each measure from the Holm family.
#   H1  ratings rise from None to Slight to Dramatic: tests 1 and 2 both
#       positive and significant;
#   H2  averaged over modification, the penalty is small or absent: test 3;
#   H3  whether the penalty changes with modification, no direction
#       predicted: test 4.
readings <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  f <- filter(family, measure == m)
  r <- setNames(f$reading, f$test)
  tibble(
    measure = m,
    hypothesis = c("H1", "H2", "H3"),
    rule = c("tests 1 and 2 both positive and significant after Holm",
             "test 3 significant after Holm (the equivalence test passes)",
             "test 4 two-sided after Holm; positive means the penalty shrinks"),
    reading = if (anyNA(r)) NA_character_ else c(
      if (all(r[c("1", "2")] == "positive and significant")) "holds" else "does not hold",
      if (r[["3"]] == "equivalent: inside plus or minus 0.224")
        "small or absent: inside plus or minus 0.224" else "not shown to be small",
      r[["4"]]))
}))

# H1 and H2 are stated over the three measures: H1 that ratings rise on all
# three, H2 that the penalty is small or absent on each. Each is read over
# the three measures as well, and it holds there only when it holds on every
# measure. H3 asks a question of each measure and has no such reading.
ACROSS <- tribble(
  ~hypothesis, ~needed,                                        ~yes,                               ~no,
  "H1",        "holds",                                        "holds on every measure",           "does not hold on every measure",
  "H2",        "small or absent: inside plus or minus 0.224",  "small or absent on every measure", "not shown to be small on every measure")
across_measures <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ACROSS)), function(i) {
  h <- ACROSS$hypothesis[i]
  r <- readings$reading[readings$hypothesis == h]
  tibble(measure = "all three measures", hypothesis = h,
         rule = paste(h, "holds on each of the three measures"),
         reading = if (anyNA(r)) NA_character_ else
           if (all(r == ACROSS$needed[i])) ACROSS$yes[i] else ACROSS$no[i])
}))
readings <- bind_rows(readings, across_measures)
stopifnot(nrow(readings) == 11)
write_csv(readings, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_hypothesis_readings.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(readings))
```

# 6. Cumulative-link checks of tests 1, 2 and 4

```{r clmm}
# A cumulative-link mixed model treats the five answers as ordered
# categories: it estimates where the cut points between neighbouring answers
# fall on an underlying scale instead of assuming the answers are evenly
# spaced. Each measure gets the registered model in that form, with the logit
# link (a logistic curve for the chance of answering above each cut point),
# the same random intercepts and the same sum-to-zero contrasts:
#
#   ordered rating ~ source x modification x image kind
#                    + (1 | participant) + (1 | source image)
#
# Tests 1, 2 and 4 are the same contrasts on the underlying scale, from
# emmeans, each with a Wald z test (the estimate divided by its standard
# error, compared with a normal distribution). The check keeps the family of
# twelve: the nine p-values from these models stand in for the linear
# model's p-values of tests 1, 2 and 4, and the three equivalence p-values of
# test 3, which this check does not cover, come from the linear model. Holm
# corrects the twelve, and each verdict on tests 1, 2 and 4 (significant or
# not, and in which direction) is set beside the linear model's.
#
# A fit counts as converged when the optimizer returns code 0 and raises no
# warning about convergence, the Hessian (the matrix of second derivatives
# the standard errors come from) or singularity, as in Study 1. It counts as
# singular when a random-effect standard deviation lies below 1e-4.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_clmm_check.csv"))

fit_clmm <- function(d) {
  d$rating_ord <- factor(d$rating, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE)
  warns <- character(0)
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch(ordinal::clmm(rating_ord ~ source * modification * image_kind +
                             (1 | id) + (1 | image),
                           data = d, link = "logit", Hess = TRUE,
                           contrasts = SUM_CONTRASTS),
             error = function(e) e),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  failed <- inherits(fit, "error")
  status <- tibble(
    fit_error = failed,
    converged = !failed && isTRUE(fit$optRes$convergence == 0) &&
      !any(grepl("converge|Hessian|singular", warns, ignore.case = TRUE)),
    singular  = if (failed) NA else
      any(vapply(ordinal::VarCorr(fit), function(m) any(attr(m, "stddev") < 1e-4),
                 logical(1))),
    lme4_messages = paste(unique(c(if (failed) conditionMessage(fit), warns)),
                          collapse = " | "))
  list(fit = fit, data = d, status = status,
       max_abs_gradient = if (failed) NA_real_ else max(abs(fit$gradient)))
}

clmm_fits <- lapply(data_by_measure, fit_clmm)
for (m in MEASURES) {
  cl <- clmm_fits[[m]]
  cat(m, "cumulative-link fit: fit error", cl$status$fit_error,
      "| converged", cl$status$converged, "| singular", cl$status$singular,
      "| largest absolute gradient", signif(cl$max_abs_gradient, 3), "\n")
}

clmm_rows <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  cl <- clmm_fits[[m]]
  base <- tibble(measure = m, test = c(1L, 2L, 4L),
                 test_name = unname(TEST_NAMES[c("1", "2", "4")]))
  if (cl$status$fit_error) {
    return(base %>% mutate(clmm_estimate = NA_real_, clmm_se = NA_real_,
                           clmm_z = NA_real_, clmm_p = NA_real_,
                           clmm_converged = FALSE, clmm_singular = NA,
                           note = fit_note(cl$status)))
  }
  ct <- four_contrasts(function(spec) emmeans::emmeans(cl$fit, spec, data = cl$data))
  base %>%
    mutate(clmm_estimate = ct$estimate[test], clmm_se = ct$se[test],
           clmm_z = ct$statistic[test],
           clmm_p = na_unless_usable(ct$p_two_sided[test], cl$status),
           clmm_converged = cl$status$converged,
           clmm_singular = cl$status$singular,
           note = fit_note(cl$status))
}))

lmm_side <- select(family, measure, test, lmm_estimate = estimate,
                   lmm_p = p_family, lmm_p_holm = p_holm,
                   lmm_holm_significant = holm_significant)
clmm_family <- bind_rows(
  clmm_rows %>% mutate(p_in_family = clmm_p, p_from = "cumulative-link model"),
  family %>% filter(test == 3) %>%
    transmute(measure, test, test_name, p_in_family = p_family,
              p_from = "linear model (equivalence test, not checked here)")) %>%
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p_in_family, method = "holm", n = N_FAMILY))
stopifnot(nrow(clmm_family) == N_FAMILY)

clmm_check <- clmm_family %>%
  filter(test != 3) %>%
  rename(clmm_p_holm = p_holm) %>%
  mutate(clmm_holm_significant = clmm_p_holm < ALPHA) %>%
  left_join(lmm_side, by = c("measure", "test")) %>%
  mutate(same_direction = sign(clmm_estimate) == sign(lmm_estimate),
         verdicts_agree = clmm_holm_significant == lmm_holm_significant &
           (!clmm_holm_significant | same_direction),
         family = "twelve: the nine cumulative-link p-values of tests 1, 2 and 4 with the linear model's three equivalence p-values, Holm",
         model = "ordered rating ~ source * modification * image_kind + (1 | id) + (1 | image), logit link, Laplace approximation, sum-to-zero contrasts; contrasts of estimated marginal means on the underlying scale, Wald z tests") %>%
  select(measure, test, test_name, clmm_estimate, clmm_se, clmm_z, clmm_p,
         clmm_p_holm, clmm_holm_significant, lmm_estimate, lmm_p, lmm_p_holm,
         lmm_holm_significant, same_direction, verdicts_agree, clmm_converged,
         clmm_singular, note, family, model) %>%
  arrange(factor(measure, levels = MEASURES), test)
stopifnot(nrow(clmm_check) == 9)
write_csv(clmm_check, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_clmm_check.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(clmm_check, measure, test, clmm_p_holm,
                           clmm_holm_significant, lmm_holm_significant,
                           verdicts_agree)), digits = 4)
```

# 7. Exploratory: the source contrast at each modification level

```{r source-by-level}
# Human minus AI at each modification level, averaged over image kind, on
# each measure, with a 95 percent interval and a two-sided t test. The
# registration lists this as exploratory, so the nine tests are not
# corrected and carry no verdict.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_source_by_modification.csv"))
source_by_level <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  res <- primary[[m]]
  if (res$status$fit_error) {
    return(tibble(measure = m, modification = MOD_LEVELS,
                  role = "exploratory, uncorrected", note = fit_note(res$status)))
  }
  ct <- emmeans::contrast(emm_of(res$fit, ~ source | modification, data_by_measure[[m]]),
                          list("Human minus AI" = c(1, -1)), adjust = "none")
  as_tibble(summary(ct, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), level = 0.95)) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character)) %>%
    transmute(measure = m, modification, contrast, estimate, se = SE, df,
              t = t.ratio,
              ci95_lo = na_unless_usable(lower.CL, res$status),
              ci95_hi = na_unless_usable(upper.CL, res$status),
              p_two_sided = na_unless_usable(p.value, res$status),
              role = "exploratory, uncorrected",
              converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
              note = fit_note(res$status))
}))
stopifnot(nrow(source_by_level) == 9)
write_csv(source_by_level, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_source_by_modification.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(source_by_level, measure, modification, estimate,
                           ci95_lo, ci95_hi, p_two_sided)), digits = 4)
```

```{r fit-status}
# One row per fit in this file: the registered model and the cumulative-link
# model, on each measure.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_fit_status.csv"))
status_row <- function(status, m, role, formula, d, gradient = NA_real_) {
  status %>% mutate(measure = m, role = role, formula = formula,
                    n_obs = nrow(d), n_participants = n_distinct(d$id),
                    n_images = n_distinct(d$image),
                    usable = fit_usable(status),
                    max_abs_gradient = gradient, .before = 1)
}
fit_status <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  bind_rows(
    status_row(primary[[m]]$status, m, "registered model", deparse1(FORMULA),
               data_by_measure[[m]]),
    status_row(clmm_fits[[m]]$status, m, "cumulative-link check",
               "ordered rating ~ source * modification * image_kind + (1 | id) + (1 | image)",
               data_by_measure[[m]], clmm_fits[[m]]$max_abs_gradient))
}))
print(as.data.frame(select(fit_status, measure, role, n_obs, fit_error,
                           converged, singular, usable)))
write_csv(fit_status, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_fit_status.csv"))
```
